summary: The layering, naming and plumbing APIs are implementable; the biggest gap is the contention and crash-recovery semantics of the WithLockedDocument lock.

questions.text: When WithLockedDocument finds the lock held, does it block, time out or refuse, and is it an OS advisory lock or a lock file that can go stale after a crash?
questions.reason: Evidence publication, clearing and reclamation from several CLI/MCP/web processes depend on it; ADR 0003 only says it 'holds the scope's exclusive lock throughout the callback' and 'Its lock file is a sibling of that directory', and ADR 0029 reuses 'the instance store lock'.

questions.text: When ReadTree meets a symlink, does it silently omit the entry or return an error?
questions.reason: Silently dropping a file changes captured draft inputs; ADR 0003 says ReadTree 'does not follow symlinks', while ADR 0006 makes symlinks in Git capture 'explicit diagnostics'.

questions.text: ADR 0003 says the EvolutionStore interpreter introduces only plumbing requirements, but ADR 0010's runEvolutionStore requires the porcelain RootStore and WorkspaceStore.
questions.reason: Import checks must know whether porcelain interpreters may require other porcelain effects; ADR 0003: 'it removes a semantic effect and introduces only plumbing requirements' vs ADR 0010: 'runEvolutionStore :: (RootStore :> es, WorkspaceStore :> es, ...)', though ADR 0003 point 3 allows lowering to 'narrower effects/plumbing'.
